tagline: Up the Oconaluftee to a gap that was found late.
intro: The byway starts where the Blue Ridge Parkway ends, at the foot of the Oconaluftee valley above Cherokee, and follows US 441 up the river past the visitor center and Smokemont. Then the road keeps climbing, through hardwood and pine-oak forest into spruce and fir, to the Tennessee line at Newfound Gap, 5,048 feet up.

The name means what it says. For years the way over was Indian Gap, two miles west, until Arnold Guyot measured these mountains in 1872 and found this pass lower. The road over it was finished in 1932.

moments.title: Oconaluftee
moments.text: Beside the visitor center stand log buildings moved here from around the park in the 1950s, set up together as the Mountain Farm Museum.

moments.title: Mingus Mill
moments.text: Water off Mingus Creek runs down a wooden flume to two turbines that turn the millstones, in a mill a Tennessee millwright built in three months in 1886.

moments.title: Newfound Gap
moments.text: The Rockefeller Memorial stands where Franklin Roosevelt dedicated the park on September 2, 1940, and the Appalachian Trail crosses the road here at the state line.

practical: The road is kept open all year except during and just after winter storms, when it can close for hours. Tractor-trailers are prohibited, and the route is not recommended for recreational vehicles or buses.
